classification.difficultyReason: Account for the inclined ground when finding interior angles, then use sine rule for height.

content.prompt:
Melissa is standing at $A$ on a path that leads to the base $B$ of a vertical flagpole.
The path is inclined at $12^\circ$ to the horizontal, and the angle of elevation of the top $T$ of the flagpole from $A$ is $34^\circ$.

spec.description: A at lower left, B to the right on the inclined path, T vertically above B; solid AB, BT and AT. Dashed horizontal guide from A to below B. Black labels A below-left, B below and T above. No printed numerical labels or angle marks.
spec.mathematics: AB inclined 12 degrees above horizontal; AT inclined 34 degrees; BT vertical. Numerical givens remain in the stem only.

answer.short: $\angle TAB=34^\circ-12^\circ=22^\circ$; $\angle ABT=90^\circ+12^\circ=102^\circ$ because the flagpole is vertical.
answer.worked:
The angle between the line of sight and the path is $\angle TAB=34^\circ-12^\circ=22^\circ$.
The flagpole is perpendicular to the horizontal, so $\angle ABT=90^\circ+12^\circ=102^\circ$.

children.prompt: Given that $AB=20\text{ m}$, find the height of the flagpole, correct to the nearest metre.
